## Requirements: Session metadata as a first-class, Session-owned work context

### Problem and current baseline
The current Nession Session DTO (`web/src/types.ts`) exposes `session_id = agent_id:session_name`, agent/name, lifecycle/attach facts, foreground command, working directory and last activity. `web/src/product/session/components/SessionDetails.tsx` shows a name/id, connectivity, window count and recency; `SessionItem` uses the tmux name as its primary identity. Users cannot describe **what the work is about**, add tags or edit its display identity independently of tmux. Workspace should expose this context without becoming a second global shell.

Product authorities: `VISION.md`, `PRINCIPLE.md`, `docs/design/product-model.md`, `docs/design/workspace.md`, `docs/design/design-system/patterns/session-item.md`, `docs/design/composition.md`. The Session is the primary active work object; Terminal is its current live surface; Workspace is contextual depth. Related, **not replaced**: #2469 (Agent Session domain/tmux ownership), #565 (MCP hosting/tool semantics), #2654 (Session Environment). No previous issue found owning the same metadata contract.

### Decision and user experience
1. **Metadata is distinct from runtime status and tmux identity.** Introduce Session-owned `title?`, `description?`, `tags: string[]` and metadata `revision/updated_at`; expose reliable `created_at` only when recorded, never synthesize it from last-activity. Keep `agent_id`, `session_name`, `session_id`, live cwd, foreground command, lifecycle, connectivity and attachment state in their existing authoritative domains. Reserve optional Workspace identity linkage for later; no Workspace database required.
2. **Title is a user-facing display alias, not tmux rename.** Empty/absent title falls back to `session_name` in Session navigation and SessionDetails; the underlying `session_id`, attach/reconnect/kill targets, shell and tmux session name stay unchanged. Do not auto-generate a title from foreground commands or AI text.
3. **Description and tags are lightweight.** Description is user-written plain text, not executable Markdown or AI policy. Tags are a simple flat list of trimmed, nonempty strings, case-insensitively unique with stable order; no colors, tag manager, hierarchy, filters-as-navigation, auto-tagging or capability-specific meaning. Define bounded lengths/counts in the shared validation contract and test invalid/overlong inputs. Initial suggested bounds: title 120 Unicode codepoints, description 2,000, up to 12 tags of 32 codepoints.
4. **Persist at Agent-owned Session domain.** Use an isolated metadata store under the Agent's private data directory (suggested `~/.nession/agent/sessions/<opaque-session-instance-id>/metadata.json`), with atomic writes and optimistic `revision` conflict handling. A persisted **instance identity** (opaque UID or equivalent proven generation fence) must survive Agent restart for an existing tmux Session, while killing and recreating the same `agent_id:session_name` must not inherit unrelated metadata. Introduce this without changing the existing route key or forcing all callers onto a new ID immediately; safely initialize legacy tmux Sessions with absent metadata.
5. **One owner, two access paths.** Agent Session domain owns metadata reads/mutations and lifetime; Server routes authorized, typed Session operations and may cache a marked last-known view, but does not invent a competing mutable metadata store. Web/App use the established Session product/API boundary. Validate Session/Agent ownership and existing authorization on both direct and relayed paths. Failed, concurrent, offline and stale writes must not claim success or overwrite another client; remain functional when the Session is detached (no current viewer).
6. **Workspace first, quiet navigation.** Extend the existing SessionDetails Workspace view: editable title, description, simple tags and minimal execution-context facts, with inline edit/save/cancel (or a small contained editor). No permanent top header/tool bar, unrelated capability tabs or ornamental cards. Session row remains compact: primary display title, optional workload/Agent/recency, degraded state when relevant; do not put tag clouds or descriptions in every navigation row. Web uses existing sidebar/Workspace composition; App uses safe-area-aware single-column Workspace depth with reachable actions/return. Editing works by keyboard and touch.
7. **Truthful states.** Loading, no metadata (legacy), saving, save success, empty title fallback, invalid tag, revision conflict, disconnected/unreachable Agent and session replacement must be distinct. Preserve unsaved edits during transient faults where safe; never silently apply a stale save to a different Session.

### Explicit deferral: Session I/O / Observation / History
**OUT OF SCOPE in this Issue:** input-history capture by Composer/Shell/Claude Code, terminal Enter parsing, output history JSONL, durable input/output event model, `.nession/sessions/<id>/history`, MCP streaming/observe/send/wait, execution-completion inference, orchestration or AI-generated metadata. These require a separate Session I/O and Observation design (Snapshot / output cursor / input / actual completion signals) that respects the existing `SessionInputState` ACK and bounded `SessionStreamState` epoch/sequence/replay semantics. #565 currently covers a read-only session preview but explicitly defers real-time I/O. Do not conflate preview with historical output. The prototype must not display a fabricated History tab.

### Proposed surface and implementation owners
- Agent `crates/nession-agent/src/session/*`: metadata lifecycle and store behind SessionService/SessionRegistry boundary; no business fields in `nession-tmux`.
- `crates/nession-protocol/src/contracts/session/*`: versioned, optional-compatible metadata read/update DTOs and error mapping, using protocol/codegen owner (#678); existing Session summaries remain backwards compatible.
- Server session routing + Web `web/src/product/session/*`: authorized read/update; SessionDetails and SessionItem presentation; App shell remains owner of depth/Back.
- Document the durable Session metadata contract in the narrowest relevant `docs/design` and `docs/architecture` owners when implementing, not as a duplicate framework.

### Prototype
- **Decision:** Required, explicitly requested. Primary uncertainty: in-place title/description/tags save/cancel, title alias versus tmux identity, tag editing, empty-metadata fallback, conflict/unavailable feedback and Web/App Workspace depth.
- **Status:** Verified on 2026-11-06. Pages direct HTML returns HTTP 200 with title “Nession · Session Metadata · Interactive Prototype #2789”; `prototypes/manifest.json` reports source SHA `527d166ae77c8ae7f56c0fc02e044a461d43d578` and the `session-metadata-2789` entry; real Chromium at 1440×900 and 390 CSS px exercised edit/save/cancel, the retained conflict draft and reload, the offline notice, and the App viewport switch with zero console errors. Durable record: `docs/design/design-system/patterns/session-metadata-2789-prototype.md`.
- **Direct HTML (verified live 2026-11-06):** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/session-metadata-2789/index.html
- **Immutable source:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/tree/527d166ae77c8ae7f56c0fc02e044a461d43d578/session-metadata-2789
- **Scenario / test notes:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/527d166ae77c8ae7f56c0fc02e044a461d43d578/session-metadata-2789/README.md
- **Gallery:** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/#/prototypes (manifest source SHA and entry verified against the prototype branch tip).
- **Scenario:** Select active Session → Workspace Session details → edit Title/Description/Tags → save → row title updates, underlying tmux name/route unchanged → cancel/edit unsaved → legacy no-metadata fallback → Agent offline save denied → stale revision conflict preserves draft until user explicitly chooses to discard and load remote state → recreate same tmux name with a distinct instance identity. Web 1180/1024 and App 430/390/375 viewport fixtures are provided.
- **Static/mock and browser verification:** the author’s V8 DOM-stub run passed **21/21** recorded interaction assertions and **7** resource/HTML assertions. Independently, real Chromium on 2026-11-06 loaded the published Pages URL with no console or page errors, edited and saved a title, kept a draft through the conflict fixture and reloaded the remote version, saw the offline notice, and switched to the 390 CSS-px App view. HTML/CSS remain approximations of the current Nession light design tokens and Session/Workspace shell, **not browser pixel-matched**; native mobile, production backend behavior and real persistence remain **unverified**. This artifact is not production Acceptance evidence for SC-01..SC-05.
- **No history/I/O UI:** The prototype deliberately contains no History tab and does not imply MCP Session observation exists.

### Verification design / scenario selection
- **SC-01 & SC-04:** SCN-03 (isolated Agent+tmux runtime, `full-stack-local` + protocol/runtime Case; restart/recreate/legacy/fault fixture, exact-SHA evidence).
- **SC-02:** SCN-01 (typed schema, authentication/bounds/revision deterministic negative tests; source + targeted Gate/Case).
- **SC-03 & SC-05:** SCN-02 (canonical Chromium+Playwright browser Case on Web desktop and App 390px, keyboard/touch, fixture state switches, actual DOM assertions).
- **SC-06:** SCN-08 (prototype branch exact file/source SHA/gallery consistency, truthful HTTPS/manifest readback; artifact evidence, not production UI proof).
Each SC has a concrete safe verifier owner; no environment secret, production deployment or main-only privilege is required for the intended PR proof.

### Success Criteria
- [x] SC-01 A Session with absent metadata renders a valid fallback; updating title/description/tags persists across Agent restart while tmux Session survives; no mutation of existing Session identity, attach, Terminal or lifecycle behavior.
- [x] SC-02 Authorized versioned metadata read/update round-trips; invalid values/unauthorized target/stale revision fail explicitly and leave prior metadata intact. Old clients/legacy Session summaries remain compatible.
- [x] SC-03 Web Workspace SessionDetails and App narrow Workspace render/read/edit/save/cancel the same metadata with accessible controls, bounded scrolling and reachable return; failures/conflicts do not masquerade as success or discard unsaved edits.
- [x] SC-04 After kill and recreate of the same tmux name, metadata from the previous Session instance is not attached to the new one; cleanup and/or retention are explicit and safe, including legacy Session and offline/reconnect handling.
- [x] SC-05 Session navigation uses the metadata title when set and otherwise the tmux name, while keeping workload/Agent/recency and degraded-state semantics; editing the display name never changes `session_id` or the actual tmux name, and unrelated list rows do not gain permanent tags/cards.
- [x] SC-06 A clickable Web/App prototype under the existing shared `prototype` branch demonstrates the complete scenario, states and reset at 1:1 viewport sizes using the shared #2758 presentation frame; gallery, immutable source pin, and verification/preview status are documented without calling the mock a production implementation.
